arguments.summary: Repository-grounded design for human-readable operator aliases on agent instances. Five implementation tasks in a DAG: (1) domain types + store interface + in-memory store, (2) MongoDB store, (3) ProductionService alias wiring + operator HTTP alias-aware resolution and CRUD endpoints, (4) CLI alias subcommands + alias-aware role operations, (5) MCP operatortools alias tools + alias-aware resolution in existing role tools. Tasks 4 and 5 are parallel with disjoint write scopes. FQN validation is never weakened; alias resolution is an additive lookup that precedes it, guaranteeing backward compatibility.

architecture: The feature introduces a local operator-facing alias layer that is architecturally separate from the existing federation alias subsystem (organization/federation.go). Federation AliasBinding carries route ID, deployment identity, and trust-grant semantics; a local RoleAlias is simply a validated short name bound to an ActorFQN. Reusing federation types would entangle operator ergonomics with cross-deployment trust and force every alias operation through federation authorization.

The resolution point is at every operator-facing transport boundary (operatorhttp, CLI, MCP operatortools), not inside ProductionService.StartRole/StopRole or other domain-level methods. This preserves the existing kernel.ActorFQN-typed service interface: the service always receives a valid ActorFQN. Resolution is adapter logic — a helper (ResolveRoleAlias) that tries kernel.ActorFQN(name) first, and if that fails, looks up the name in a RoleAliasStore. If neither path yields a valid FQN, the adapter returns an error. This guarantees zero behavioral change for callers that already pass FQNs.

The ProductionService gains a RoleAliasStore field (organization.RoleAliasStore interface) and four additive methods — SetRoleAlias, UnsetRoleAlias, ListRoleAliases, ResolveRoleAlias — in a new file (role_alias_service.go) to avoid modifying the already-1500-line production.go beyond the single struct field addition. These methods are exposed through the operator HTTP interface as new Service interface methods and through a new operatortools Organization interface group.

The operator HTTP handler (adapters/operatorhttp/handler.go) routing is extended with /v1/role-aliases CRUD routes. In the existing /v1/roles/<operand>/<action> and /v1/roles/<operand>/inbox paths, the roleControl and roleInbox methods insert an alias-resolution step before the FQN validation gate. The deadLetters path (query parameter actor) receives the same treatment. The FQN validation kernel.ActorFQN(parts[0]).Valid() remains the guard; resolution merely produces a valid FQN string from an alias before the check.

The CLI (cmd/tekroo/main.go) gains an 'alias' subcommand family (set/unset/list) that calls the new HTTP endpoints, and existing 'role', 'inbox', and 'deadletters' commands gain alias resolution by calling a resolve endpoint (GET /v1/role-aliases/<name>) before making their primary call. The usage string and roleOperation/actorRead helper signatures are updated.

The MCP operatortools Service (adapters/operatortools/service.go) gains three new tool names (tekroo.role.alias.set, tekroo.role.alias.unset, tekroo.role.alias.list) and a resolver that runs before the existing role-control tool handlers call Organization.StartRole etc. The MCP handler (adapters/mcp/handler.go) registers the new tool schemas. The Organization interface in operatortools gains the four alias methods, which ProductionService satisfies structurally.
assumptions: Local operator aliases are set at runtime via the new endpoints/tools; no static config-seeded alias list is required by the specification.
Alias names share the same character class as federation alias names (lowercase alphanumeric, hyphen, dot, max 64 chars) but are stored and validated in a separate namespace.
A given alias maps to at most one ActorFQN at a time; re-setting an alias overwrites the previous binding (operator is responsible for re-binding).
No alias hierarchy, wildcards, or team-level aliasing is needed; the operator story asks for a flat 1:1 name→FQN mapping.

design_decisions.rationale: Federation AliasBinding is bound to route_id, route_revision, and deployment_identity with federation authorization semantics. A local operator alias has no route or deployment concern. Coupling them would force every local alias operation through federation trust checks and make the federation test surface a dependency of trivial operator ergonomics.

design_decisions.decision: Resolve aliases at the transport boundary, not inside ProductionService domain methods
design_decisions.rationale: Every operator path (operatorhttp handler, CLI, MCP operatortools) already parses a string into kernel.ActorFQN before calling service methods. Adding resolution at this single point per path (4 sites) is lower-risk than modifying the service interface signature to accept untyped strings and resolving internally, which would blur the boundary between validated FQN identity and raw user input.

design_decisions.decision: New file role_alias_service.go for ProductionService alias methods
design_decisions.rationale: production.go is already approximately 1500 lines. Adding 4 methods (Set/Unset/List/Resolve) plus their wiring there would make the file harder to review. The new file is the same package (operationalruntime) so the methods are accessible with zero import changes; only the struct field addition goes into production.go.

design_decisions.decision: Alias resolution helper in organization package as a free function, not a method on a new type
design_decisions.rationale: The resolution logic is two lines: try FQN parse, else store lookup. Wrapping it in a dedicated resolver type adds indirection without testability gain. A package-level function that accepts a RoleAliasStore parameter is composable at every call site without requiring a new field on each adapter.

tasks.description:
Add alias management subcommands and alias-aware resolution to the tekroo CLI binary.

**CLI subcommand design:**
- `tekroo -config <c> alias set <name> <actor-fqn>` → POST /v1/role-aliases with body `{"name":"<name>","actor_fqn":"<actor-fqn>"}`.
- `tekroo -config <c> alias unset <name>` → DELETE /v1/role-aliases/<name>.
- `tekroo -config <c> alias list` → GET /v1/role-aliases.
- `tekroo -config <c> alias resolve <name>` → GET /v1/role-aliases/<name>, prints resolved FQN.

**Resolution in role/inbox/deadletters:**
- In `roleOperation` (line 223), before FQN validation of `operands[0]`, if `kernel.ActorFQN(operands[0]).Valid()` is false, issue GET /v1/role-aliases/<operands[0]> to the daemon; on 200, extract actor_fqn and proceed with that FQN. On 404, fall through to usageError.
- Same pattern in `actorRead` (line 256) for the inbox path and in the `deadletters` command's optional actor operand.
- A `resolveOrFQN` helper in cmd/tekroo/main.go encapsulates the FQN-parse-then-alias-resolve pattern used by all three sites.

The usage error string (line 618) gains `alias set|unset|list|resolve` in the command list.

tasks.title: MCP and operatortools alias tools and alias-aware resolution

arguments.summary: Repository-grounded design for human-readable operator aliases on agent instances. Five implementation tasks in a DAG: (1) domain types + store interface + in-memory store, (2) MongoDB store, (3) ProductionService alias wiring + operator HTTP alias-aware resolution and CRUD endpoints, (4) CLI alias subcommands + alias-aware role operations, (5) MCP operatortools alias tools + alias-aware resolution in existing role tools. Tasks 4 and 5 are parallel with disjoint write scopes. FQN validation is never weakened; alias resolution is an additive lookup that precedes it, guaranteeing backward compatibility.

architecture: The feature introduces a local operator-facing alias layer that is architecturally separate from the existing federation alias subsystem (organization/federation.go). Federation AliasBinding carries route ID, deployment identity, and trust-grant semantics; a local RoleAlias is simply a validated short name bound to an ActorFQN. Reusing federation types would entangle operator ergonomics with cross-deployment trust and force every alias operation through federation authorization.

The resolution point is at every operator-facing transport boundary (operatorhttp, CLI, MCP operatortools), not inside ProductionService.StartRole/StopRole or other domain-level methods. This preserves the existing kernel.ActorFQN-typed service interface: the service always receives a valid ActorFQN. Resolution is adapter logic — a helper (ResolveRoleAlias) that tries kernel.ActorFQN(name) first, and if that fails, looks up the name in a RoleAliasStore. If neither path yields a valid FQN, the adapter returns an error. This guarantees zero behavioral change for callers that already pass FQNs.

The ProductionService gains a RoleAliasStore field (organization.RoleAliasStore interface) and four additive methods — SetRoleAlias, UnsetRoleAlias, ListRoleAliases, ResolveRoleAlias — in a new file (role_alias_service.go) to avoid modifying the already-1500-line production.go beyond the single struct field addition. These methods are exposed through the operator HTTP interface as new Service interface methods and through a new operatortools Organization interface group.

The operator HTTP handler (adapters/operatorhttp/handler.go) routing is extended with /v1/role-aliases CRUD routes. In the existing /v1/roles/<operand>/<action> and /v1/roles/<operand>/inbox paths, the roleControl and roleInbox methods insert an alias-resolution step before the FQN validation gate. The deadLetters path (query parameter actor) receives the same treatment. The FQN validation kernel.ActorFQN(parts[0]).Valid() remains the guard; resolution merely produces a valid FQN string from an alias before the check.

The CLI (cmd/tekroo/main.go) gains an 'alias' subcommand family (set/unset/list/resolve) that calls the new HTTP endpoints, and existing 'role', 'inbox', and 'deadletters' commands gain alias resolution by calling a resolve endpoint (GET /v1/role-aliases/<name>) before making their primary call. The usage string and roleOperation/actorRead helper signatures are updated.

The MCP operatortools Service (adapters/operatortools/service.go) gains three new tool names (tekroo.role.alias.set, tekroo.role.alias.unset, tekroo.role.alias.list) and a resolver that runs before the existing role-control tool handlers call Organization.StartRole etc. The MCP handler (adapters/mcp/handler.go) registers the new tool schemas. The Organization interface in operatortools gains the four alias methods, which ProductionService satisfies structurally.
assumptions: Local operator aliases are set at runtime via the new endpoints/tools; no static config-seeded alias list is required by the specification.
Alias names share the same character class as federation alias names (lowercase alphanumeric, hyphen, dot, max 64 chars) but are stored and validated in a separate namespace.
A given alias maps to at most one ActorFQN at a time; re-setting an alias overwrites the previous binding (operator is responsible for re-binding).
No alias hierarchy, wildcards, or team-level aliasing is needed; the operator story asks for a flat 1:1 name to FQN mapping.

design_decisions.rationale: Federation AliasBinding is bound to route_id, route_revision, and deployment_identity with federation authorization semantics. A local operator alias has no route or deployment concern. Coupling them would force every local alias operation through federation trust checks and make the federation test surface a dependency of trivial operator ergonomics.

design_decisions.decision: Resolve aliases at the transport boundary, not inside ProductionService domain methods
design_decisions.rationale: Every operator path (operatorhttp handler, CLI, MCP operatortools) already parses a string into kernel.ActorFQN before calling service methods. Adding resolution at this single point per path (4 sites) is lower-risk than modifying the service interface signature to accept untyped strings and resolving internally, which would blur the boundary between validated FQN identity and raw user input.

design_decisions.decision: New file role_alias_service.go for ProductionService alias methods
design_decisions.rationale: production.go is already approximately 1500 lines. Adding 4 methods (Set/Unset/List/Resolve) plus their wiring there would make the file harder to review. The new file is the same package (operationalruntime) so the methods are accessible with zero import changes; only the struct field addition goes into production.go.

design_decisions.decision: Alias resolution helper in organization package as a free function, not a method on a new type
design_decisions.rationale: The resolution logic is two lines: try FQN parse, else store lookup. Wrapping it in a dedicated resolver type adds indirection without testability gain. A package-level function that accepts a RoleAliasStore parameter is composable at every call site without requiring a new field on each adapter.

CLI subcommand design:
- tekroo -config <c> alias set <name> <actor-fqn> sends POST /v1/role-aliases with body {"name":"<name>","actor_fqn":"<actor-fqn>"}.
- tekroo -config <c> alias unset <name> sends DELETE /v1/role-aliases/<name>.
- tekroo -config <c> alias list sends GET /v1/role-aliases.
- tekroo -config <c> alias resolve <name> sends GET /v1/role-aliases/<name>, prints resolved FQN.
